about: Java mutation plan: one entry per shard (the shard number is the 1-based position). Built from the PIT histories of full run 42472119807 (mutants per class and method, covering tests per mutant) and the measured per-mutant time of full run 42838755118 with one JVM per mutant (est_min assumes no savings from cheaper JVMs, 30% over the measured rate, a pessimistic rate for the shards that did not finish): every slice <= 190 min except single methods that cannot be split further. exclude_methods are exact method names of the same class; the last shard (rest) takes every class that is not listed, so a new class is mutated too. v2: shards 72, 19, 17, 41, 23, 31 and 22 were cancelled at the job limit in 42902111378 (their per-test cost was far above the model): each is split into parts of about 45 model minutes, the first part keeps the shard number and the others are appended after the rest shard. v3: Pq$Suite (7 mutants) is deliberately left to the catch-all rest shard, so that shard is never empty (the shared shard report refuses an empty shard). v4: shard 99 (GoalSemantics, 906 mutants) was cancelled at 355 min in 42956714806 at a measured 29.5 s/mutant (shard 98: 715 mutants took 351 min): split into 4 parts of ~227 mutants (~110 min at that rate). v5: the 0.5 classes (Prohibitions 2,500+ mutants, Contracts, ContractEnforcer, ForbidWins, Risk, Beacons, Taint) all fell to the catch-all rest shard, which was cancelled at 355 min in 43181227130 after 3,381 mutants (about 6.3 s per mutant): they get their own shards 125-130, Prohibitions split by method in three (lambdas, <init> and <clinit> go to the third). v6: the 0.5 agent-side classes (Facade with its nested types, Catalog, SignersMore, ProducerOps) fell to the rest shard, which was cancelled at the job limit in 43523228514: they get their own shards 131-134 (Facade itself, Facade's nested types with Catalog, SignersMore, ProducerOps). v7: SignersMore and ProducerOps were cancelled at the job limit in 43584279559 (their tests sign with every PQ suite, so a mutant costs far more than the model): SignersMore is split by method in four, ProducerOps in three (run; prim and b64; the rest); each method's lambdas go with it; the first parts keep shards 133 and 134, the others are 135-139. v8: the slices of one class now partition it: Issue.envelopeError, Issue.headers and Issue.signPCActn (0.5 methods named in neither Issue exclude list) were mutated by both shard 46 and shard 82, and ProducerOps.ed, edSuite, pq and suite by all three ProducerOps shards; they now stay only in shard 82 and in the ProducerOps rest shard 139. v9: positions 140-144 are placeholders for the adapter module shards of the workflow (they name no class), so a core slice can follow them; the 0.6 core classes MeshFederation, PqQuorum, SafetyCertificate, Zk / ZkCeremony / ZkBundled, Kem and Entropy / EntropyError get their own shards 145-149 instead of the catch-all rest shard (a class pattern ending in * also takes the nested types; est_min and mutants are 0 until a full run measures them). v10: shard 98 (GoalSemantics.applies+22, 715 mutants) was cancelled at the job limit in 45514582120 after about 590 mutants (about 36 s of wall time per mutant with four JVMs, its covering tests grew since v4): split by PIT mutator in four (non-void calls; argument propagation and negate; remove-conditionals and constants; the rest), est_min at that rate; the first part keeps shard 98 and the others are 150-152. v11: (a) the workflow now applies mut, mutators and mutators_except (before, the v10 split ran every mutator in all four parts); (b) slices predicted over 60 model minutes are split by PIT mutator group (mut: n = NON_VOID_METHOD_CALLS; c = negate/boundary/experimental; r = remove-conditionals and INLINE_CONSTS; x = every other mutator, the complement of n, c and r in the workflow's ALL list) in two or three parts that partition the slice exactly; est_min and mutants of a part are the slice's shares (40/26/21/13 percent, from the GoalSemantics split); (c) the 0.6 classes that no slice named (every package outside the verifier core, about 125689 lines in 521 files) were all in the catch-all rest shard: they are cut into slices 153-280 of about 1200 lines each (class names and their nested types, no pattern wider than one file), est_min at 20 minutes per 1000 lines (the Kotlin shards measured 5-97, median 20) and mutants at 0.25 per line, both UNMEASURED until a full run; the first part of a split keeps its shard number, all new slices are appended after 152 (matrix 1 holds shards up to 256, matrix 2 the rest).
